messages.subject: facet_grid() and position_dodge() scaling issue
parts:
Hi,

i am aware of the recent post on the facet_grid problem, but i ran into a related problem.
The following example is a breakdown of my code to illustrate the issue and the output figure is attached.

I am using geom_errorbar() and facet_grid() quite a lot and i recently discovered, that if a facet has less datapoints, the errorbars width changes.
I tried to use scale='free_y' to avoid the free scaling of the width along the x-axis, but even then, due to use of position_dodge(), the width is scaled, at least in parts of the figure (see the right figure).

I don't see a meaningful reason for scaling the width in case of additional use of position_dodge(). Is it unintended?

Is there any possibility to avoid the width scaling of geom_errorbar() so i can use 'free' as well as 'fixed' scaling in facet_grid()?

Thanks and best wishes,
Herbert

----------
zz <- "group step  label intensity timep sd n age_range_index
1      1    3 a        10 0.0222160 0.003354945 50 1
2      1    3 b        10 0.0568040 0.009785348 50 1
3      1    4 a        30 0.0192720 0.002773713 50 1
4      1    4 b        30 0.0535980 0.009303466 50 1
5      1    5 a       100 0.0163420 0.003176514 50 1
6      1    5 b       100 0.0513140 0.009071620 50 1
7      2    3 a        10 0.0261175 0.003462094 40 1
8      2    3 b        10 0.0510900 0.003898047 40 1
9      2    4 a        30 0.0241800 0.003428029 40 2
10     2    4 b        30 0.0475800 0.003644891 40 2
11     2    5 a       100 0.0204125 0.004562961 40 2
12     2    5 b       100 0.0436450 0.003559095 40 2"

df <- read.table(text=zz, header = TRUE)
df$fact_col = factor(df$group, levels=c(1, 2), labels=c('N', 'P'), ordered=TRUE)
df$age_str <- factor(df$age_range_index, levels=c(1:2), labels=c('young', 'old'), ordered=TRUE)
print(df)

xlstr <- expression('Intensity (log cd*s/' * m^2 * ')')
ylstr <- expression('Time (ms)')
barwidth <- 0.2

p <- ggplot(df) + geom_point(aes(log10(intensity), timep*1000,
                colour=fact_col), position=position_dodge(width=0.2), shape=16)
p <- p + scale_x_continuous(name=xlstr) + scale_y_continuous(name=ylstr)
p <- p + scale_colour_manual('', values=c('red', 'green'), guide='legend')
p <- p + geom_errorbar(aes(x=log10(intensity), ymax=(timep+sd)*1000, ymin=(timep-sd)*1000,
                colour=fact_col), position=position_dodge(width=0.2), width=barwidth)

q <- p + facet_grid(label ~ age_str, space="fixed", scales="free")
r <- p + facet_grid(label ~ age_str, space="fixed", scales="fixed")
s <- arrangeGrob(q, r, ncol=2)

#grid.draw(s)
ggsave(file='geom_errorbar_problem.jpg', plot=s, width=10, height=4)
--------

parts:
I guess I would characterize the issue in exactly the opposite way;
the width is not scaled, (i.e., it is .02 in all facets) and you would
like it to be (i.e., you would like it to be scaled so that it appears
visually consistent, though this requires the numeric values to differ
from one facet to the next. Is that right?

--Ista

messages.author: ff42271ef6191bca
messages.subject: Re: facet_grid() and position_dodge() scaling issue
parts:
Thanks. You are right, i thought it should appear consistent, but it working as designed.
My understanding of how position_dodge works was wrong. I thought it would calculate a fixed offset for a group of data which would be identical for all facets.
But it is not. I prepared another figure to illustrate the problem. For this i changed the x-values and just added two additional data rows for the facet young & label "a" (top left). Now the plot is inconsistent, because position_dodge forces a change of the width of the errorbars while shifting x-values. Now the group "N" values of the "young" for label "a" and "b" are no longer aligned on the x-axis.

I assumed that position_dodge would determine the x-offsets considerung all values from all facets to always give consistent results in all facets. In this case, the width would automatically be visually consitent (if using scales="fixed"). But it uses only values for a given x-value in the actual facet (remark: it takes all values into account regardless if they will be plotted or are outside the limits).

Is there any general solution?

Best,
Herbert
